info.title: Kenning Trusted Agent API
info.description: Agent Guard evaluates and records proposed agent actions before execution. It does not execute shell commands, SQL, filesystem operations, or cloud mutations. Requests use tenant-scoped product-managed Bearer personal access tokens on the public API, or AWS SigV4 on an AWS_IAM workload API. The workload API maps a verified IAM role to a tenant-configured agent and bounded scopes.

bearerAuth.description: Send Authorization: Bearer kta_pat_... for product-managed PATs, kta_agent_... for short-lived agent credentials, or a tenant-configured RS256 OIDC/OAuth 2.0 token. PATs and agent credentials are tenant-scoped, hashed at rest, and can expire or be revoked. Federated tokens must pass issuer or introspection, audience where configured, expiry, tenant, subject, and configured scope checks. PATs that ingest external audit events require audit:write.

awsIamAuth.name: Authorization
awsIamAuth.description: AWS API Gateway must verify the request with AWS_IAM authorization and SigV4. Swagger UI does not generate SigV4 requests; use the signed invocation helper in scripts/invoke_workload_identity.py. Include X-Kenning-Tenant-Id so Kenning can select the tenant workload-identity mapping.

sessionCookie.name: kta_session
sessionCookie.description: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=None browser session cookie. It is created by POST /auth/session or the configured OIDC callback and is never exposed to browser JavaScript.

provider.description: Integration provider supplied by the caller, such as GitHub. Guard uses it to select provider-specific normalization before generic risk detection.

action_id.description: Stable caller-supplied action identifier. Retries with the same semantic action return the original decision, approval, proof, and receipt; reusing it for a different action returns 409.

classification.description: Optional NZ Government sensitivity classification. Guard compares levels in ordinal order for classification-aware policies.

purpose.description: Optional data-use purpose used by consent-aware policies.

data_scope.description: Optional data scope used by consent-aware policies.

provider.description: Optional provider metadata when the action is sent through a generic tool shape.

model_id.description: Registered AI model used by the bound agent, or null when the registered agent is unbound.

model_version.description: Resolved version of the registered AI model, or null when unbound.

model_risk_tier.description: Risk tier resolved from the registered model, or null when no registered model is available.

intent.description: User or system intent supplied with the action; Guard uses it as context and does not treat it as authorization.

target.description: Resource, path, database, or target identifier.

parameters.description: Adapter-specific parameters. Common risk context includes reversible, requested_scope, affected_resource_count, resource_count, and estimated_rows. Shell actions may provide command or executable plus args/arguments, cwd/working_directory, env/environment_variables, and execution_context for inspection; secret-valued environment fields are redacted. Financial actions that expose payment, payout, invoice, bank, transfer, charge, refund, or transaction context with mutating intent receive the FINANCIAL_TRANSACTION reason code and require approval; read-only financial lookups are not escalated by this signal.

adapter.description: Provider adapter selected by Guard when provider-specific context is available.

adapter_context.description: Provider-specific context preserved alongside the common action model.

ShellContext.description: Inspectable shell execution context. Secret-valued environment fields are redacted before persistence or response.

arguments.description: Command arguments supplied separately from the executable.

requested_scope.description: Resource IDs or scope declared by the calling agent.

intent.description: User or system intent the agent is trying to fulfil.

approval_id.description: Original operator approval ID when resuming an approved action. Must be paired with action_hash and the unchanged action_id.

action_hash.description: Original semantic action hash returned by Guard when resuming an approved action.

message.example: DELETE or UPDATE statement has no WHERE clause.

action_hash.description: SHA-256 of the semantic normalized action. Generated run_id, action_id, and requested_at correlation metadata are excluded; the approval still binds the action_id and tenant separately.

approver_principal.description: Authenticated non-secret principal that approved the action. For OIDC this is the verified subject; for PATs it is the token or agent identity metadata ID.

approver_auth_source.description: Authentication source used for the approval, such as oidc, pat, or agent.

approval_requirements.description: Every listed requirement must be satisfied by the approver's verified group membership; groups within one requirement are alternatives.

triggering_rule.description: Summary of the rule that triggered this approval, captured at creation time. Absent for approvals created before this field existed.

rule_source.description: Whether the winning rule is a Kenning built-in default or a workspace policy.

selected_rule.description: The most-restrictive winning rule from policy resolution.

matched_rules.description: Every rule that matched the action, applied or not.

approval_chain.description: Multi-step approval chain definition (#245), present when the triggering rule requires sequential sign-off.

chain_steps.description: Per-step status for a multi-step approval chain. Each step tracks its own status, approver, and decision time.

current_step.description: The 1-based step that is currently actionable in a multi-step chain.

total_steps.description: Total number of steps in the approval chain.

evidence.description: Redacted evidence associated with the evaluated action.

Grant.description: A duration-based approval grant. Auto-approves every action matching the bound action hash until it expires or is revoked.

action_hash.description: Semantic action hash this grant matches.

source_approval_id.description: The approval whose approval created this grant.

use_count.description: How many actions have been auto-approved under this grant.

signature.description: Optional service signature. Deployed AWS environments use KMS RSA-PSS; local dependency-free tests may use HMAC-SHA256.

action_classification.description: Normalized classification recorded for the evaluated action.

idempotent.description: True when a retry returned the existing durable decision for the same action_id and semantic action hash.

identity.description: Identity delegation result when the action's agent is registered.

approval_creation_latency_ms.description: Internal elapsed time from the approval decision branch until the approval record, including Proof references, is durably written.

audit_acceptance_latency_ms.description: Internal elapsed time for the decision audit event to be durably accepted by the configured audit store.

model_id.description: Registered AI model used by the bound agent, or null when the agent is unbound.

model_version.description: Resolved version of the registered AI model, or null when unbound.

simulation_source.description: Source used by policy simulation. Historical sources are tenant-scoped recorded action evaluations.

tenant_policy.description: Tenant and environment controls applied before built-in Guard rules.

audit_delivery.description: Best-effort external audit sink status. The Guard decision is already durable before delivery is attempted.

GuardUnavailableResponse.description: Fail-closed response returned when Guard cannot complete evaluation or durable recording. The caller must not execute the action.

approver.description: Optional display label. The authenticated principal is recorded separately; a federated OIDC caller must use its verified subject.

action_hash.description: Optional assertion that the approval request still refers to the exact evaluated action.

grant_duration.description: Optional duration in seconds for a duration-based grant. When set on an approve decision, creates a grant that auto-approves identical actions for this window. Bounded by a server-side maximum of 14400 (4 hours); values above the maximum are ignored.

step.description: For multi-step approval chains, the 1-based step being decided. Must match the current actionable step; out-of-order decisions return 409.

revoked_by.description: Optional human or system actor label; the authenticated subject or PAT is used by default.

reason.description: Why the pending or approved authorization is being revoked.

approval_id.description: Required when the original Guard decision required human approval.

result.description: Tool result or a redacted result summary.

tenant_id.description: Optional tenant assertion; it must match the authenticated tenant unless the token has admin scope.

idempotency_key.description: Stable retry key. It may also be supplied as the Idempotency-Key header.

TokenMetadata.description: Metadata for a PAT. The plaintext token and token hash are never included.

groups.description: Reviewer or workload groups carried by this token; delegated tokens cannot add groups their issuer does not possess.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp; omitted for a non-expiring token.

tenant_id.description: Optional tenant assertion; it must match the authenticated tenant unless the caller has admin scope.

scopes.description: Scopes to delegate. A non-admin caller may only delegate scopes its issuer possesses.

groups.description: Optional reviewer or workload groups. Omitted groups are inherited; a non-admin caller may only delegate groups it already has.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime in days. Zero creates a non-expiring POC token.

approver_groups.description: For require_approval rules, groups within this list are alternative reviewer groups. The approver must have a verified membership in one group for every matching requirement.

conditions.description: Supported conditions include environment, resource/target, agent_id, user/invoked_by, tool, operation/action_type, provider, region, start_time/end_time or time_window, amount thresholds, query_scope, maximum_scope, reversible, dry_run_required, requires_consent, and requires_impact_assessment. requires_consent is an object with purpose and data_scope; a matching active consent prevents the rule from applying. The impact-assessment condition is a warn-only reminder when the agent has no completed assessment from the last 365 days.

PolicyResolution.description: Deterministic explanation of how matching policy rules were compared and which rule selected the effective policy decision.

PolicySimulationRequest.description: Simulate a supplied action or replay a tenant-scoped historical action evaluation. Exactly one source is required.

source_action_id.description: Action ID of a previously recorded action.evaluated event in the caller's tenant.

StarterRuleSimulationRequest.description: Simulate one configured starter rule against a supplied action without executing it.

compliance_tags.description: Optional tenant-managed Privacy Act or Algorithm Charter labels used for coverage summaries.

last_reviewed_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent manual policy review.

test_cases.description: Reusable non-executing test cases to run before publication.

confirm.description: Must be true to perform the requested lifecycle change.

review_overdue.description: True when the policy has never been reviewed or the last review is more than 365 days old.

test_cases.description: Optional ad hoc cases; when omitted, cases stored on the policy version are run.

model_id.description: Optional registered AI model bound to this agent.

model_version.description: Resolved model version for the agent binding.

parent_agent_id.description: Optional parent agent for agent-to-agent delegation. A parent must be the authenticated agent credential or the caller must have platform-admin scope.

maximum_authority.description: Maximum authority this agent may exercise. Child agents cannot exceed their parent's level.

can_delegate_agents.description: Allows this agent to register child agents when authenticated with an identity:write agent credential.

not_before.description: Delegation is denied before this instant.

not_after.description: Delegation is denied after this instant.

delegation_chain.description: Non-secret principals and parent agents that created this identity, from root to immediate delegator.

impact_assessment_status.description: Whether the agent has a completed internal impact assessment from the last 365 days.

documentation_completeness.description: Completed life-cycle documentation sections out of four.

token.description: Returned once. Store it securely; it cannot be retrieved later.

claim_type.description: Optional claim category used to select a tenant-specific quality or currency threshold.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the bounded retrieved source bytes or supplied inline source text.

source_hash_verified.description: Whether the supplied source_hash matched content_sha256.

source_verified.description: Whether the source exists, was accessible, and passed the authenticity check.

source_score.description: Source verification score based only on existence, accessibility, and authenticity.

claim_support_score.description: Claim-to-source support score. Unsupported claims score 0 even when the source itself is real.

confidence.description: Claim-support confidence from 0 to 1. Unsupported, failed, or inaccessible citations return 0; source verification is reported separately.

claim_support_required.description: Whether this citation has a claim that should be compared with the retrieved source.

reference_verified.description: Whether supplied bibliography metadata matched the retrieved source. Null when no bibliography metadata was supplied or the source could not be retrieved.

retrieval_status.description: Transport outcome for the source retrieval. A transport error means the source could not be assessed from the verifier network path; it does not prove that the URL is invalid.

retrieval_attempts.description: Number of bounded source retrieval attempts made.

retrieval_strategy.description: Transport path that succeeded. node_fetcher means the private Kenning regional fetcher Lambda retrieved the source.

retrieval_via.description: Reserved for a bounded intermediary URL when an explicitly configured source transport uses one.

retrieval_diagnostics.description: Bounded non-secret diagnostics for failed or recovered retrieval attempts.

policy_scope.description: Effective tenant citation thresholds after applying the claim-type override, if any.

response.description: The agent response to inspect for citations.

claim_type.description: Optional category such as legal, financial, or operational.

source_hash.description: Optional SHA-256 digest, with or without the sha256: prefix, that binds the citation to exact source content.

claim_support_required.description: Set false for source-only checks such as bibliography or metadata URLs.

reference_metadata.description: Parsed bibliography metadata to compare with the retrieved source.

reference_sources.description: Optional source metadata used to resolve extracted document, identifier, and footnote references.

trust_score.description: Average claim-support score for claim-bearing citations and source verification score for source-only citations. Source and bibliography metadata verification remain separately reported on each finding.

report_text.description: Deterministic text extracted from the report. The browser portal extracts PDF text locally before calling this endpoint.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the UTF-8 report_text.

category.description: Report context classification. Non-claim categories are source-checked without claim entailment.

claim_support_required.description: Whether the extracted context is a claim that should be compared with the retrieved source.

resolution_reason.description: How the marker was resolved to a bibliography URL, or why it remains unresolved.

ProofInput.description: A source document or input reference. Raw content is hashed and removed from stored proof records.

claim.example: Supplier A has the lowest total cost

secret_arn.description: Secrets Manager ARN containing the sink bearer token. The secret must be tenant-owned under kenning/audit-sinks/{environment}/{tenant_id}/; raw tokens are never accepted here.

validation_mode.description: JWT validates RS256 signatures through JWKS; introspection validates opaque OAuth 2.0 access tokens through the configured endpoint.

introspection_url.description: HTTPS OAuth 2.0 token-introspection endpoint; required when validation_mode is introspection.

client_id.description: OAuth client ID used for introspection.

client_secret_arn.description: Tenant-scoped Secrets Manager ARN under kenning/tenants/{tenant_id}/oauth/ containing the OAuth introspection client secret; the secret value is never stored in tenant configuration.

groups_claim.description: JWT claim containing reviewer or workload group names.

allowed_subjects.description: Optional exact or wildcard subject patterns for users or workload identities.

WorkloadIdentity.description: AWS IAM role-to-agent mappings used only behind an API Gateway route configured with AWS_IAM authorization. Unmapped, ambiguous, and out-of-account roles are denied.

principal_arn.description: Exact IAM role ARN or a role-path pattern containing * or ?. Assumed-role session context is canonicalised to this role ARN before matching.

CitationPolicy.description: Tenant controls for Citation Trust source retrieval, freshness, and optional source-quality thresholds. Source quality is reported as metadata and is not included in the default score.

allowed_domains.description: Optional host or wildcard host allowlist.

trusted_domains.description: Optional first-party host or wildcard host patterns. Matching sources are classified as primary; this is metadata unless a minimum source-quality policy is configured.

allow_inline_source_text.description: Allow callers to provide source_text for controlled verification tests.

respect_robots.description: Check the source host robots.txt before retrieving content. Set false only for a tenant with explicit authority to bypass robots directives.

robots_fail_closed.description: Block retrieval when robots.txt cannot be retrieved or is otherwise unavailable, including HTTP 401 or 403 responses.

claim_type_policies.description: Optional per-claim-type overrides for source quality and currency thresholds.

legal_hold_enabled.description: Prevent retention execution and remove existing DynamoDB TTL markers for retained records.

legal_hold_reason.description: Required explanation when legal_hold_enabled is true.

data_residency_region.description: AWS deployment region for tenant data. This deployment accepts only its own configured region.

starter_rules.description: Tenant-owned copy of the deterministic Guard starter rules. Omitted rules are removed for this tenant.

CapturePolicy.description: Controls which normalized action fields are retained or returned. Guard evaluation and the raw action hash remain unchanged.

store_original_action.description: Retain the original action payload inside the captured action record.

redact_fields.description: Dot-delimited action paths replaced with a tenant-policy redaction marker.

hash_fields.description: Dot-delimited action paths replaced with deterministic sha256 values. Paths cannot overlap redact_fields.

max_field_length.description: Maximum captured string length before truncation.

TenantSummary.description: Safe tenant registry metadata. Detailed policy, identity-provider, audit-sink, and capture configuration remains tenant-scoped.

tenant_id.description: The authenticated tenant for a non-admin caller; null when a platform admin lists all tenants.
